clue.text: Mates have this day to finish the vessel

parts.note: Fri is the standard short form of Friday
to finish is to end
a ship is a seagoing vessel

explanation.surface: A crew is given one day to get a boat built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mates' looks like ship's officers, in keeping with the vessel, but it means friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Close companions share a bond of mutual affection, which is what the word names.

clue.text: Sorry, the plant's not quite complete

parts.note: rue is a bitter herb, a garden plant

indicators.note: not quite means the word for complete loses its final letter

parts.note: full means complete

explanation.surface: Apologising that a garden plant has not fully grown.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sorry and regretful, expressing remorse.

clue.text: From English trees, initially, create bats and similar things

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of trees
bats, meaning crazy, signals that the letters of create are scrambled

explanation.surface: Making cricket bats and the like from English timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the willow bats made from trees, but it means crazy, an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'and the rest', used to mean other like items.

clue.text: Provider of quiet service that's useful for moveable feasts

definitions.text: Provider of quiet service that's useful for moveable feasts

parts.words: Provider of quiet service that's useful for moveable feasts
parts.note: a silent server: a small lift carrying food between floors, so meals literally move

explanation.definitionFit: A small goods lift that carries dishes between kitchen and dining room, a mute server.

clue.text: They live alone, a woman's writing about it

parts.note: her means belonging to a woman

indicators.note: about means the writing letters go around the word it

parts.note: MS stands for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Solitary people, says a woman writing on the subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Recluses who withdraw from society to dwell in solitude.

clue.text: Feed people — those in favour

definitions.meaning: read as fee'd people: professionals, who are paid fees
the arguments or people supporting something

explanation.definitionFit: Short for professionals, paid experts, and also the supporters in pros and cons.

clue.text: What Marian achieved if entering partnership with Robin

indicators.note: entering means the word if goes inside the word for partnership

parts.note: we, the pronoun for a couple or partnership
Robin Hood, the outlaw of English legend

explanation.surface: Maid Marian's success depended on teaming up with Robin.
explanation.walkthrough: Maid Marian is Robin Hood's sweetheart in the legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrying her outlaw lover gave Marian the married state of a spouse.

clue.text: Is stolen pound put in my case in error?

indicators.note: put in means the stolen pieces are placed within another word
case means the word my forms the outer casing

parts.note: taken means stolen
L is the symbol for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Has someone wrongly placed stolen money into my briefcase?
explanation.walkthrough: 'my case' suggests luggage; it means the word MY acts as a case around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Done by mistake, wrongly or erroneously.

clue.text: Italian resort has the edge fashionable one the Romans used

parts.note: a rim is an edge or border
in means in fashion
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A trendy Italian seaside town boasts an old Roman connection.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimini is a well-known beach town on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Late arrival runs after one of Thackeray's heroes

indicators.note: after places the runs letter at the end, following the hero's name

parts.note: Colonel Newcome is the hero of Thackeray's novel The Newcomes
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone arriving late dashes after a character from a Victorian novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' here means recent, not tardy: a recent arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has only lately arrived is a recent incomer to a place or group.

clue.text: Wrong maiden is taken to celebration

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
a treat is a special celebration or outing

explanation.surface: A young woman is wrongly escorted to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' is a verb here, to do wrong by someone, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrong someone is to abuse or ill-use them, a verb of harmful handling.

clue.text: Not quite quick enough to escape?

indicators.note: not quite means the word for quick loses its final letter

parts.note: fleet means quick or swift

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they are too slow to get away.
explanation.definitionFit: To escape is to run away from danger, to take flight.

clue.text: Foreign money I check for supposedly poor friar

parts.note: the franc was the currency of France and other countries
to scan is to check or examine

explanation.surface: Checking foreign cash for a monk who claims poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supposedly poor' because the order takes vows of poverty.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the order founded by St Francis, whose friars vow poverty.

clue.text: Dessert wine's no great shakes

parts.note: afters is British slang for dessert, the course after the main meal
hock is a white Rhine wine

explanation.surface: A sweet wine served with pudding turns out to be unremarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no great shakes' normally means mediocre; here it is read literally as a lesser tremor.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor following an earthquake is smaller than the main quake, so its shaking is not great.

clue.text: Place to get dressed, boy, and smarten up

parts.note: Robin is a boy's name
to groom is to smarten one's appearance

explanation.surface: A lad is sent to a dressing area to tidy himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A room where officials or clergy put on their formal robes or vestments.

clue.text: A new poet appears moderately quickly

parts.note: Dante Alighieri is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A fresh poet arrives on the scene at a steady pace.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the term is a tempo marking for a moderate walking pace.

clue.text: Sounds like Alice's cat might blow up

indicators.note: sounds like signals the answer is spoken the same as the phrase

parts.note: Dinah is Alice's cat in Lewis Carroll's books, followed by might

explanation.surface: A girl's pet might explode, so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to destroy with explosives, to blast.

clue.text: Lack of inhibition of some players in performance

parts.note: a band is a group of musical players
on means performing, as in being on stage

explanation.surface: Some musicians lose all restraint while playing a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild, uninhibited freedom of behaviour, as in dancing with gay abandon.

clue.text: Oriental capital I held, possibly

parts.note: read as an instruction, the answer asks for a fresh arrangement of the city name, giving these two words

explanation.surface: Someone may once have occupied an Eastern capital.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: NEW signals an anagram of DELHI, and that anagram is 'I held'; 'possibly' marks the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of India, in the East.

clue.text: Rapid changes in pitch — six bowled at Oval without runs

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral for six
B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled

indicators.note: without means outside, so the word at sits within the other letters

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
O is oval in shape; the Oval is also a London cricket ground

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a six, a bowler's wicket, but no runs at the Oval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without runs' reads as scoring none; here 'without' means outside. The Oval is a London cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulsating effect in music made by fast fluctuations of a note.

clue.text: Try improvement, for a change

definitions.meaning: in rugby, the kick after a try that adds two more points
a transformation from one form or belief to another

explanation.definitionFit: Rugby's post-try kick and any transformation of form or faith share one name.

clue.text: Like strong thread that's twisted round one

indicators.note: round means the twisted word goes about the letter for one

parts.note: wry means twisted or contorted
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tough strand of thread has been wound around something.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thin, tough and sinewy resembles strong wire or cord.

clue.text: Dismiss a class

definitions.meaning: to sack someone or take them from office
at some British public schools the ... is the name of a form, a school class

explanation.definitionFit: To oust from a post; also a form name at some English schools.

clue.text: See term's been rearranged as this, possibly

definitions.text: See term's been rearranged as this, possibly

indicators.note: rearranged tells us to reorder the letters of the words see and terms

explanation.surface: Notice that the school term has been reorganised into a new format.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'term's' counts as a letter of the fodder; the whole clue doubles as the definition, since the result is a kind of term.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-year teaching period in colleges is one possible form of academic term.

clue.text: Most of the capital of an Asian country

indicators.note: most of means the word the loses its last letter

parts.note: capital means first-rate, A1, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Most of the capital city belongs to an Asian nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city, but it is the exclamation 'Capital!', meaning excellent or A1.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to Thailand, the Southeast Asian nation.

clue.text: Devilish name Silver had to shoulder?

parts.note: Long John Silver in Treasure Island kept a parrot, a polly, perched on him
on, as the parrot sat on the pirate's shoulder

explanation.surface: Asks what devilish name the pirate Silver was forced to bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had to shoulder' suggests burden; read it as Silver had a Polly (parrot) on his shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: In Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress and in Revelation, this is a name of the Devil, the destroyer.

clue.text: Scan the American theatre for her double appearance

indicators.note: to scan is to look closely along the words, where a girl's name lies concealed

explanation.surface: Look over the US stage for a woman who appears twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double appearance' because the name is concealed twice: in 'scan the A' and in 'American theatre'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthea is a woman's given name, so 'her' points to a female name.

clue.text: Club first used as instrument of torture

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
maiden means first, as in a maiden voyage

explanation.surface: A cudgel was the first thing used to torment victims.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval spiked cabinet in which a victim was enclosed, a device for torment.
